title: Deadly Tank Explosion Could Have Been Prevented
summary:
A terrible accident happened at a paper mill in Washington state. In May, a huge chemical tank burst, killing 11 workers. Now, investigators found that the tank was known to be unsafe for 10 months before it failed!

An inspection company checked the tank in July 2025 and said it was "not fit for continued service." They told the paper mill, Nippon Dynawave Packaging Company, that it needed repairs. But the company didn't do anything about it.

The tank held a liquid called "white liquor" that's used to make paper. It can cause severe burns. When it burst, it released about 900,000 gallons of this liquid—enough to blow out building walls!

The U.S. Chemical Safety Board is investigating. They said the company didn't fix the tank or even take it out of service. The inspection report said there was "significant thinning" in the tank's walls, meaning they were too thin to be safe.

A lawyer for the families of two brothers who died said the findings are "nothing short of alarming." He said, "When safety inspections and recommendations don't lead to action, danger becomes a reality that causes devastation to human life."

Senator Patty Murray said, "Every worker has the right to come home safely at the end of the day."

The company said they are cooperating with the investigation and focusing on supporting the families. But many people are asking: why wasn't this fixed before it was too late?
why_it_matters: This matters because everyone deserves to be safe at work, and this story shows what can happen when warnings are ignored.

background_read: Paper mills are factories that turn wood into paper, and they use strong liquids like 'white liquor' to help break down the wood.
Nippon Dynawave Packaging Company (the company that owns the mill) was told by inspectors in July 2025 that its tank needed repairs.
The U.S. Chemical Safety Board (a government agency that studies chemical accidents) is now investigating why the repairs were never made.
Article_Structure: WHO: Workers at the Nippon Dynawave Packaging Company, their families, inspectors, investigators, and Senator Patty Murray.
WHAT: A chemical tank that was known to be unsafe for 10 months burst and killed 11 workers.
WHERE: A paper mill in Washington state.
WHY: Because the company did not fix the tank or take it out of service after inspectors said it was not fit to keep using.
